# Unequal vertex volumes on the integer base 2 Delta_n

This note combines the proved equal-endpoint edge credit with ordinary
fiber centroids. It proves the desired OC constant for this particular
integer projection in every n>=3 and d>=1, even with unequal vertex
volumes. It also gives an actual convex-body realization showing that
these scalar certificates alone do not close the n=2 case. No statement
about arbitrary integer projections is inferred.

## 1. The actual base and all available point certificates

Write p_0=0 and p_i=e_i for 1<=i<=n. The integer points of 2 Delta_n are
exactly its N=n+1 vertices 2p_i and its binomial(N,2) edge midpoints
p_i+p_j. Suppose a convex body has this projection and every listed fiber
is a d-dimensional convex body of positive volume. Let the vertex-fiber
volumes be v_i and the midpoint-fiber volumes be k_ij. Put

    M=sum_i v_i+sum_(i<j) k_ij,
    Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.

Actual convexity gives, for every edge,

    (A_i+A_j)/2 subset K_ij,
    k_ij >= [(v_i^(1/d)+v_j^(1/d))/2]^d.                (1)

The ordinary centroid of any single fiber belongs to the full mixed set
and guarantees at least Gamma_d times its own volume in every containing
ambient halfspace. If a halfspace is constant on that fiber it contains
the entire fiber; otherwise ordinary Grunbaum applies to its trace.
Other fibers contribute nonnegative mass. Thus each of the numbers
Gamma_d v_i and Gamma_d k_ij is an actual point certificate.

There is also an actual edge certificate. Put m_ij=min(v_i,v_j). Shrink
the larger endpoint body homothetically about its ordinary centroid to
volume m_ij, and keep the smaller endpoint. Convexity ensures this
trimmed body is contained in the original one, its centroid is unchanged,
and its midpoint body with the other endpoint remains inside K_ij.
The proved all-dimensional dominated-centroid theorem and equal-volume
coupling therefore give a point in K_ij whose depth in the ORIGINAL set
is strictly greater than

    (3/4) Gamma_d (k_ij+m_ij).                         (2)

The affine parametrization of the chosen base edge transports every
ambient halfspace to an affine halfspace with the appropriate two
endpoint offsets. If the restriction is constant, a containing ambient
halfspace contains all three fibers and the claim is immediate. No
unimodular transformation of the full lattice is being asserted or needed: the produced center has the actual integer
base p_i+p_j, and its three fibers are subsets of the original set.
The uniform strict gap follows from the positive dual gap and the fixed
interior ball at the dominated centroid, as in the audited edge theorem.

Define the scalar certificate size

    B=max{ max_i v_i, max_(i<j) k_ij,
               (3/4)max_(i<j)[k_ij+min(v_i,v_j)] }.     (3)

At least Gamma_d B is guaranteed at one of finitely many deterministic
actual points. When the maximum in (3) is achieved by an edge expression,
the guarantee at that edge point is strict.

## 2. A sharp complete-graph mass inequality

For arbitrary nonnegative vertex and edge numbers, with B defined by(3),

    M <= [(3N^2-N+4)/6] B.                             (4)

Here N>=2 and B>0. The bound is sharp even when all the actual midpoint
Brunn–Minkowski inequalities(1) are imposed.

**Proof.** Scale B to1 and relabel so 1>=v_1>=...>=v_N>=0. For i<j,

    k_ij<=min(1,4/3-v_j).

Consequently

    M<=v_1+sum_(j=2)^N [v_j+(j-1)min(1,4/3-v_j)].

For any t in[0,1], the j-th bracket is at most j-2/3. If t<=1/3 this
follows from t+(j-1)<=j-2/3. If t>=1/3 its value is
4(j-1)/3-(j-2)t, again at most j-2/3 because j>=2. Therefore

    M<=1+sum_(j=2)^N(j-2/3)=(3N^2-N+4)/6.

For sharpness take v_1=1, v_2=...=v_N=1/3 and all k_ij=1. Then B=1
and equality holds. Every volume root in(1) is at most1, so all those
inequalities hold in every dimension d. Section4 realizes these numbers
by an actual convex body. QED.

## 3. Consequence in every n>=3

At N=4 the coefficient in(4) is8=2^(N-1). For N>=4 it is at most
2^(N-1); an elementary induction uses

    2(3N^2-N+4)/6 - [3(N+1)^2-(N+1)+4]/6
        =(3N-1)(N-2)/6>0.

Therefore M<=2^n B for every n>=3. The actual certificate(3) proves

    max_(y in S) depth_S(y) >= Gamma_d/2^n.             (5)

In fact the inequality is strict for this positive-volume projection
class. For n>3 the combinatorial inequality is already strict. For n=3,
if M<8B it is again strict. If M=8B, equality in the bracket bound forces
v_3=v_4=B/3 and k_13=k_14=B, so an edge expression in(3) equals B.
Its actual guarantee(2) is strict. This covers the remaining equality
case without claiming that an ordinary simplex centroid bound is strict.

This theorem assumes the complete positive-volume base 2 Delta_n. It
does not handle missing fibers, arbitrary lattice polytopes, intrinsic
lower-dimensional intersections, or arbitrary n=2 fibers by itself.
For d=0 the arbitrary-volume menus in this note do not describe counting
measure; that separate pure-integer case is not included implicitly.

## 4. An actual n=2 obstruction to these scalar certificates

For n=2 the sharp menu in Section2 is

    (v_1,v_2,v_3)=(1,1/3,1/3),
    k_12=k_13=k_23=1.

Then

    M=14/3,  B=1,  M/2^n=7/6>1.                      (6)

Thus neither the largest individual-fiber centroid certificate nor any
homothetically trimmed edge certificate reaches the requested total-mass
constant on these data. The strictness in(2) has no quantified margin
large enough in the stated theorem to fill the gap1/6.

These numbers are not merely a formal Brunn–Minkowski menu. Fix a
convex body D in R^d of volume1 containing zero in its interior. At the
first vertex place D; at every other vertex place 3^(-1/d)D; at every
edge midpoint place D. Let C be the convex hull of all these fibers over
the corresponding bases in 2 Delta_n. It is compact and convex and has
full affine dimension n+d, hence nonempty ambient interior.

Every vertex of the projected simplex is exposed, so its actual fiber
is exactly the assigned body. Every edge midpoint lies in the relative
interior of a projected simplex edge. Any convex combination projecting
there can use only bases on that edge. All three assigned bodies on
that edge are contained in D, and the midpoint already carries all of D.
Thus the actual midpoint fiber is exactly D. The projection has no
other integer points. This proves exact realization, including every
compatibility constraint and every fiber volume in(6).

It is only a counterexample to the sufficiency of the listed scalar
certificates. It is not a counterexample to OC: other centers, actual
additional captured masses from the remaining fibers, and stronger edge
inequalities are not bounded above by(3).
